stem: Hours after the birth of a baby boy, the observant mother noticed that he became cyanotic anytime he cried vigorously. What is the embryological explanation and prognosis for this condition?

options.label: A
options.text: There has been a coarctation of the baby’s aorta

options.label: B
options.text: Vigorous crying opens a patent ductus venosus

options.label: C
options.text: Vigorous crying increases the pressure in the right atrium that temporary opens a yet-to-fuse septum primum

options.label: D
options.text: Surgery is required to correct the defect causing the problem

options.label: E
options.text: Survival rate is very high for babies with this condition

disputed_statements: Transient cyanosis with crying and a prognosis of high survival.
proposed_interpretation: A transient right-to-left atrial shunt is possible if right atrial pressure rises above left atrial pressure. The stem does not establish an isolated patent foramen ovale.
reason: Recurrent visible cyanosis hours after delivery has other serious causes. Prognosis and the need for intervention cannot be inferred from crying alone.
ask_lecturer: Is the case intended to establish an otherwise healthy newborn with an isolated patent foramen ovale confirmed on assessment?

stem: Which of the following veins does NOT contribute to the formation of the inferior vena cava?
disputed_statements: Whether the right posterior cardinal vein forms part of the inferior vena cava proper.
proposed_interpretation: The right umbilical vein regresses without forming the cava. The posterior cardinal system supplies the common iliac veins and their confluence, variably described as a caudal caval contribution.
reason: With a strict definition limited to segments of the inferior vena cava proper, the right posterior cardinal vein is also a plausible exception.
sources: NCBI Bookshelf, Anatomy, Abdomen and Pelvis: Inferior Vena Cava https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK482353/
Congenital anomalies of the IVC—embryological perspective and clinical relevance https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5220208/
ask_lecturer: Does the course include the iliac confluence in its definition of the inferior vena cava?

stem: Concerning lung development and function, as well as medico-legal cases, evaluate the following

options.label: A
options.text: Lungs from a newborn baby who died before birth will float when placed in water

options.label: B
options.text: Lungs of newborn who died after birth will sink when placed in water

options.label: C
options.text: The lungs are totally non-functional in the foetus

options.label: E
options.text: Respiratory distress syndrome results from lack of surfactant-secreting cells in the epithelium of the lungs

options.label: F
options.text: Congenital lobar emphysema results from lack of pneumocyte type I cells in the epithelium of the lungs

disputed_statements: The assertion that respiratory distress syndrome results from lack of surfactant-secreting cells is keyed true.
proposed_interpretation: Premature lungs usually contain immature type II pneumocytes with insufficient surfactant production. Cell absence and functional immaturity have different meanings.
reason: The stored explanation changes the assertion from absent cells to insufficient surfactant. Flotation also reflects aeration and cannot independently establish live birth.
ask_lecturer: Does “lack of surfactant-secreting cells” mean immature cells with inadequate secretion, and should the forensic limits of flotation be explicit?
